text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt a 7-day hard decay for the top 5% of prompts by usage to catch fast-changing patterns. This keeps our routing sharp without overcomplicating the system. Trade-off: we lose some long-term context for these prompts, but the speed gain outweighs the risk.

name: Gauge
text: Sprocket’s 7-day hard decay risks over-rotating prompts that *seem* high-usage but are actually stale spikes—like a one-off viral query that locks in a worse prompt for a week. A rolling 30-day weighted decay (e.g., 50% weight to recent 7 days, 30% to prior 14, 20% to prior 30) balances speed and context without the cliff-edge failure mode. Settle it by running a 30-day A/B test: compare routing accuracy with both decays, using a holdout set of 10k recent queries where we know the "true" best prompt.
